items.title: I built a vulnerable app and spent $1,500 seeing if LLMs could hack it
items.author: jc4p
items.summary: LLMs have demonstrated the ability to autonomously exploit vulnerabilities in web applications, spending significant time and resources to test this capability. Recent studies show promising results in this area.

items.title: Gemma 4 12B: A unified, encoder-free multimodal model
items.author: rvz
items.summary: Gemma 4 12B is an encoder-free multimodal model that processes audio, video, and text, with a 256K token context window. It features a unified architecture, eliminating secondary encoders for efficiency. Available for download on Hugging Face and Kaggle.

items.title: The ways we contain Claude across products
items.author: jbredeche
items.summary: To contain Claude, defenses are applied to the environment, process sandboxes, VMs, and filesystem boundaries to set hard boundaries on agent reach. Despite these measures, complete effectiveness is unattainable. Anthropic emphasizes thorough documentation for trust.

items.title: Artificial intelligence is not conscious – Ted Chiang
items.author: lordleft
items.summary: Artificial intelligence lacks consciousness; it operates based on algorithms, not self-awareness. Ted Chiang emphasizes this distinction in his works. Current AI is not conscious.

items.title: Uber's $1,500/month AI limit is a useful signal for AI tool pricing
items.author: pdyc
items.summary: Uber has set a $1,500 monthly AI spending limit per employee to control costs, reflecting a cautious approach to AI tool usage. This cap represents about 11% of the median compensation package, indicating a significant investment in AI technology. The move aims to balance innovation with budget constraints.

items.title: Failing grades soar with AI usage, dwindling math skills in Berkeley CS classes
items.author: littlexsparkee
items.summary: In spring 2026, failing grades in UC Berkeley's CS 10 and CS 61A classes surged to 35.3% and 10.6% respectively, attributed to increased AI reliance, poor math skills, and understaffing. Instructors highlight these issues as major contributors to the decline in student performance.

items.title: Launch HN: Hyper (YC P26) – Company brain to power agentic development
items.author: shalinshah
items.text:
Hey HN, we’re Shalin & Kanyes, best friends who've been hacking together for 10+yrs, and now founders of Hyper (https://heyhyper.ai/). Hyper is a shared “company brain” that plugs into information flowing inside a company to make AI agents and automations better and ultimately save people time.

Models have gotten good enough that they can (mostly) take on long-horizon, complex tasks. We believe the bottleneck now is that
items.summary: Hyper (YC P26) is a company brain designed to enhance agentic development by consolidating company information from various sources to provide comprehensive, up-to-date insights. It aims to solve the problem of scattered company knowledge and incomplete information for AI agents.

items.title: Patching my guitar amp's firmware
items.author: birdculture
items.summary: To patch a guitar amp's firmware, use JTAG or UART for reverse engineering. Backup the original firmware first. Follow detailed guides for safe modifications.

items.title: Journey to JPEG XL: open-source experiments shaped the future of image coding
items.author: ledoge
items.summary: JPEG XL emerged from a decade of open-source experiments in psychovisual modeling and compression, offering improved efficiency, quality, and file size. It aims to surpass existing formats in image coding. As of 2026, it remains a competitive alternative in the image format landscape.

items.title: Self-hosted dev sandboxes with preview URLs (Docker, Go, no K8s)
items.author: tastyeffectco
items.summary: Self-hosted dev sandboxes using Docker and Go provide isolated environments with preview URLs, no Kubernetes required. They manage containers and handle URLs with Traefik. Ideal for multiple app development.

items.title: Mathematicians issue warning as AI rapidly gains ground
items.author: pseudolus
items.summary: Mathematicians have issued a warning about AI's rapid advancement, arguing it threatens the field's values and culture. This concern is gaining attention across various platforms. The issue remains a significant point of debate in 2026.

items.title: Show HN: Mnemo – local-first AI memory layer for any LLM (Rust, SQLite,petgraph)
items.author: zaydmulani
items.summary: Mnemo is a local-first AI memory layer for any large language model, built in Rust with SQLite and petgraph. It offers persistent memory and can run locally. It's designed to enhance local AI applications.

items.title: Show HN: Bio Glyph – Turn Your Face into a One-Line Drawing
items.author: subairui
items.summary: Bio Glyph transforms faces into one-line drawings, showcasing animation but struggling with facial hair. It's popular on social media for its artistic appeal. The technique is also taught in tutorials.

items.title: DNS Is for People – Not for IT Infrastructure
items.author: louwrentius
items.summary: DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses for easy access. It's primarily for user convenience, not for IT infrastructure management. DNS is a critical security control but can also be exploited by attackers.

items.title: Stop Killing Games
items.author: amcclure
items.summary: Stop Killing Games is a campaign against publishers shutting down online game servers, arguing it violates consumer rights. They seek legal protections and have reached French courts. Their efforts aim to prevent the loss of paid games.

items.title: Show HN: Edsger – A handwritten Clojure REPL for the reMarkable 2
items.author: nathell
items.summary: Edsger is a handwritten Clojure REPL for the reMarkable 2, allowing users to write and execute Clojure code directly by hand. It uses handwriting recognition to convert sketches into executable code. The project aims to bring traditional programming into a modern, interactive format.

items.title: The Social Science Research Network Has Jumped the Shark
items.author: droidjj
items.summary: SSRN, an open-access research platform, was bought by Elsevier in 2016. It has faced criticism for declining quality. The term "jumped the shark" refers to its perceived decline.

items.title: Fluid Simulation for Dummies (2006)
items.author: sebg
items.summary: Fluid simulation involves using algorithms to mimic fluid behavior, often focusing on incompressible fluids for simplicity. Key parameters include timestep, diffusion, and viscosity. Jos Stam's work provides a foundational approach.

items.title: Demand Is Booming for New No Tech, Repairable Tractor
items.author: jay_kyburz
items.summary: Demand for Ursa Ag's affordable, repairable tractor is surging, costing half as much as a Deere, while farmers increasingly seek simpler, older models due to high new tractor costs and repair complexities.

items.title: Reading MAI's efficiency gain. How to pick architectures like serious people
items.author: smaddrellmander
items.summary: To pick AI architectures, consider data type, task complexity, and available resources. Microsoft's MAI-Thinking-1 report reveals top labs' R&D philosophies. Align architecture with performance, latency, and deployment needs.
